subject: Priv GPU sizing: headroom metrics, surge scenarios, and proposed provisioning agreement
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private GPU pool: target throughput and uplift scenarios

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team wanted to align on concrete commitments so our procurement and infra teams can finish the network/hosting sign-off. High level asks from Acme: 

- Sustained throughput target: 60k embeddings/sec equivalent (p50 latency target 60ms).
- Burst profile: 3x sustained for windows up to 5 minutes (expected weekly spikes).
- Failover: regional fallback to hosted only acceptable for <=10% of traffic.

Can you share a short provisioning plan that maps these targets to GPU counts, headroom assumptions, and expected egress/network requirements? If you have a template MOU or provisioning appendix we can plug into procurement, that would help.

Attachments: traffic-shape-samples.csv (example call patterns).

Appreciate quick turnaround — procurement needs a draft by end of week to hit our fiscal window.

Thanks,
Alex Green
Infra Lead, Acme Corp

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: target throughput and uplift scenarios

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic sample. Quick clarifying Qs before we produce the provisioning appendix: 

1) Do the 60k embeddings/sec represent concurrent token throughput or batched embedding calls per second? (We model these differently.)
2) Are you expecting tensor-level KV cache reuse between calls (i.e., many repeated prefixes) or mostly independent short queries?
3) Any specific egress constraints (per-minute aggregate or sustained across peering)?

We’ll draft a proposal that includes: baseline GPU count, warm-pool sizing for burst, admission policy for graceful degradation, and preferred fallback policy language. Laura and Markus will add network and SLA notes.

-Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-08-10T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: target throughput and uplift scenarios

Alex — answering Jonas and starting a rough sizing sketch below. High-level assumptions (please confirm):

- "Embedding call" = one call with batching possible up to 64 items; average batch size expected 8 (from your CSV).
- Typical call footprint ~ 0.9 GPU-ms per item at our optimized kernel on A100/H100 equivalent (median profile).
- Network egress per embedding ~ 0.8 KB (small).

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- Sustained 60k embeddings/sec * 0.9 GPU-ms = 54k GPU-ms/sec = 54 GPU-seconds/sec.
- That maps to ~54 GPUs if single-threaded with no batching benefits; with batching (avg batch 8) we reduce to ~7–8 effective GPUs.
- Add warm-pool headroom for 3x burst for 5 minutes: we recommend warm-pool capacity sized to absorb 2.5x sustained (to keep admission mild) and an elastic slab for the remaining delta. Practically: baseline 8 GPUs, warm-pool 12 GPUs, elastic slab 20 GPUs for bursts.

Network and egress: plan for sustained peer bandwidth of 200 Mbps, burstable to 800 Mbps for the 5-minute windows. If Acme has strict egress caps, we can provide token-level samples to compress payloads.

Operational callouts:
- Cache-warmup: pre-warming strategy on deploy and scheduled warm periods (cron-based warmers).
- Admission: shed lowest-priority calls after 2x p99 latency threshold; failover to Redwood hosted API as negotiated.
- Telemetry: token-level SLOs, cost per 1k embeddings, and tracing for heavy tails.

I’ll attach a runbook draft and provisioning appendix for procurement to review.

-Laura
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-11T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: headroom and network constraints

Couple of networking cautions to surface (to align with Acme infra):

- NIC oversubscription: if Acme allocates >4x oversub per GPU host, packet drops during bursts will create artificial latency spikes. Recommend 1.5–2x oversub and explicit MTU confirm.
- Peering: prefer private peering (VPC/VPN) with BGP and QoS tagging for traffic prioritization. Public NAT egress will complicate failover SLAs.
- Egress budgeting: we'll include an explicit egress SLA and a mitigation ladder; step 1: API-level compression, step 2: reduce top-k returned tokens, step 3: progressive degradation.

I’ve updated the runbook with these items — attaching network checklist.

-Markus
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Priv GPU sizing: headroom metrics, surge scenarios, and proposed provisioning agreement

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement and infra need. Confirming answers to Jonas’ Qs:

1) The 60k figure is measured as embedding calls/sec (post-batching) — batches average 6–9 in production.
2) Calls are largely independent; prefix reuse is uncommon.
3) Egress constraint: our peering window supports sustained 400 Mbps, but procurement needs the mitigation ladder documented.

Procurement request: can you provide the provisioning appendix as a PDF and a short MOU clause that pins the warm-pool sizing and the fallback behavior? We want the appendix in a format we can attach to the SOW.

Appreciate the team moving quickly.

Alex
Infra Lead, Acme Corp

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-08-12T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv GPU sizing: headroom metrics, surge scenarios, and proposed provisioning agreement

Alex — attaching the provisioning appendix (acme_provision_template_v2.pdf) and a short MOU clause we've used with similar customers. Highlights: 

- Baseline: 8 dedicated GPUs sized for average batched throughput.
- Warm-pool: 12 GPUs kept hot (fast warm-up) to cover most bursts with an elastic slab up to additional 20 GPUs on a 60s provisioning window.
- Admission & fallback: progressive degradation with hosted fallback for up to 10% of calls; explicit OOB telemetry and a 30-day review cadence to tune headroom.

Next steps: procurement can mark up the MOU; ops will schedule a 45-minute runbook review so we can walk the checklist (network MTU, BGP, QoS, warmup jobs). Proposed slot: 2027-08-18 15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
